nodes.statement:
Although we do not have a formal proof of that,

nodes.name: Huber contamination model
nodes.statement:
It assumes that
there is a reference distribution $\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\mu}$, parameterized by $\boldsymbol\mu\in\mathcal M$, 
the precise value of which is unknown, and a contamination distribution $\mathbf Q$, 
which is completely unknown. The data points $Y_i$, $i=1,\ldots,n$ are independent random variables drawn from the mixture distribution $\mathbf P_{\epsilon,\boldsymbol\mu,\mathbf Q} = 
(1-\epsilon)\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\mu}+\epsilon\,\mathbf Q$, where $\epsilon\in[0,1]$ is the rate
of contamination.
nodes.statement_short: Data are i.i.d. from the mixture $(1-\epsilon)P_\mu+\epsilon Q$ with unknown contamination distribution $Q$.

nodes.name: Heterogeneous-outlier contamination model
nodes.statement:
We suggest here to consider an alternative model for the outliers. In the general
setting, it corresponds to considering the number of outliers, $s$, as a 
deterministic value and to assuming that the outliers $\{Y_i:i\in O\}$ (where
$O\subset [n]$ is of cardinality $s$) are independent and satisfy $Y_i\sim 
\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\mu_i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Deterministic number $s$ of outliers, each independently drawn from its own $P_{\mu_i}$.

nodes.name: Inlier mean and translation-invariant family
nodes.statement:
In addition, let $\boldsymbol\mu$ be the mean of $\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\mu}$ and the family $\{\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\mu}\} $ be translation invariant (meaning that for every 
vector $\boldsymbol a$, the random variable $\boldsymbol Y\!_i-\boldsymbol a$ is drawn from $\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\mu_i-\boldsymbol a}$).

nodes.name: Iterative bias-correction strategy for robust mean estimation
nodes.statement:
If we have an 
initial estimator $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_0$ of $\boldsymbol\mu$, which is consistent but not necessarily 
rate-optimal, then we can define the centered observations $\boldsymbol Y\!'_i = \boldsymbol Y\!_i-\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_0$. 
Each observation $\boldsymbol Y\!'_i$ will have a distribution close to $\mathbf P_{\boldsymbol\theta_i}$, where 
$\{\boldsymbol\theta_i\triangleq \boldsymbol\mu_i-\boldsymbol\mu,i\in[n]\}$ is a sparse set of vectors, 
so that $\frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]} \boldsymbol Y\!_i$ is a natural estimator of $\boldsymbol\mu+\frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]} \boldsymbol\theta_i$. The strategy we propose here
is to use an estimator $\widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n$---based on the transformed observations $\boldsymbol Y\!_i'$--- of the linear functional $\boldsymbol L_n = 
\frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]} \boldsymbol\theta_i$ and then to update the estimator of $\boldsymbol\mu$ 
by the formula
$\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_1 = \frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]} \boldsymbol Y\!_i - \widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n$. This procedure can be
iterated using $ \widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_1$ as an initial estimator of $\boldsymbol\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Center data with an initial mean estimate, estimate the linear functional of the sparse shifts, subtract it from the sample mean, and iterate.

nodes.name: Center observations
nodes.statement:
If we have an 
initial estimator $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_0$ of $\boldsymbol\mu$, which is consistent but not necessarily 
rate-optimal, then we can define the centered observations $\boldsymbol Y\!'_i = \boldsymbol Y\!_i-\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the initial mean estimate from each observation.

nodes.name: Estimate the linear functional
nodes.statement:
The strategy we propose here
is to use an estimator $\widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n$---based on the transformed observations $\boldsymbol Y\!_i'$--- of the linear functional $\boldsymbol L_n = 
\frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]} \boldsymbol\theta_i$
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $L_n=\frac1n\sum\theta_i$ from the centered data.

by the formula
$\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_1 = \frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]} \boldsymbol Y\!_i - \widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the functional estimate from the sample mean.

nodes.name: Column-sparse Gaussian matrix model
nodes.statement:
We assume that we are given a $p\times n$ matrix $\mathbf Y$ generated by the following model:
\begin{equation} \mathbf Y = \mathbf\Theta+\sigma\boldsymbol\Xi, \quad \xi_{i,j} \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,1).
\end{equation}
This means that the deterministic matrix $\mathbf\Theta$ is observed in Gaussian white noise of variance $\sigma^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Observe $\mathbf Y=\Theta+\sigma\Xi$ with i.i.d. standard Gaussian noise entries.

Column-wise Gaussian observation model
nodes.statement: \boldsymbol Y\!_i = \boldsymbol\theta_i+\sigma\boldsymbol\xi_i, \quad \boldsymbol\xi_i \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(\mathbf 0_p,\mathbf I_p),\quad i=1,\ldots,n.

nodes.name: Estimation of the multidimensional linear functional L(Theta)
nodes.statement:
Our goal is to estimate the vector $\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta)\in\mathbb R^p$, where $\boldsymbol L:\mathbb R^{p\times n}\to\mathbb R^p$ is the
linear transformation defined by
\begin{equation} \boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n \boldsymbol\theta_{i} = \mathbf\Theta\bf1_n.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $L(\Theta)=\sum_i\theta_i\in\mathbb R^p$ from the noisy matrix $\mathbf Y$.

nodes.name: Linear functional L(Theta) (L)
nodes.statement: \boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n \boldsymbol\theta_{i} = \mathbf\Theta\bf1_n.
nodes.label: L

nodes.statement:

shown to be

\end{equation}
conclusions: \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \|\widehat{\boldsymbol L}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta)\|_2^2 = \sigma^2 np.

nodes.name: Group hard thresholding optimization problem

computing the sum of the remaining signals. This is equivalent to solving

\begin{equation} \widehat{\mathbf\Theta}{}^{\rm GHT} =
	\arg\min_{\mathbf T} \Big\{ \|\mathbf Y-{\mathbf T}\|_F^2 + \lambda^2 \sum_{i=1}^n
	\mathds{1}_{\boldsymbol t_i\neq\mathbf 0} \Big\},
\end{equation}
where $\lambda>0$ is a tuning parameter.

The first inequality is a consequence of the fact that when all the entries of
$\boldsymbol\Theta$ are zero, the optimal estimator of $\boldsymbol\mu$ in the minimax sense is the

estimator of $\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Theta)$. We can associate with $\widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n$
the following estimator of $\boldsymbol\mu$: $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}(\widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n) = \boldsymbol L_n(\mathbf Y)
-\widehat{\boldsymbol L}_n$. These estimators satisfy
\begin{align}

proposition follows.

nodes.name: Risk bound of the iterative soft thresholding estimator
nodes.statement:
Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $N\in\mathbb N$ and let $\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm IST}_n(N)$ 
be the iterative soft thresholding estimator obtaind after $N$ iterations. 
Assume that $p\ge \log(8/\delta)$ and $N\ge \log\log p$. There are some universal 
strictly positive constants $c_1,c_2,c_3$ such that if the condition
\begin{align}
s\le c_1 n
\end{align}
is satisfied then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the following inequalities hold
true:
\begin{align}
\|\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm IST}_n(N)-\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Theta)\|_2
	&\le c_2\sigma\bigg\{p^{1/2}\Big(\frac{s^2}{n^2}\Big)^{1-2^{-N}}+
	\frac{s+\sqrt{sp}}{n}\bigg\},\\
\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}{}^{\rm IST}-\boldsymbol\mu\|_2
	&\le c_3\sigma\bigg\{p^{1/2}\Big(\frac{s^2}{n^2}\Big)^{1-2^{-N}}+
	\frac{s}{n}+\Big(\frac{p}{n}\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\}.
\end{align}

nodes.name: IST as approximation of a nonconvex Huber-type estimator
nodes.statement:
From an intuitive point of view, the algorithm described in \Cref{algo:3} can be
seen as an iterative approximation of the estimator
\begin{align} \widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}^*\in\text{arg}\min_{\boldsymbol\mu\in\mathbb R^p} \sum_{i=1}^n \rho_{\rm H}
\Bigg(\frac{(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i-\boldsymbol\mu\|_2^2-\sigma^2p)^{1/2}_+}{\sigma\gamma}\Bigg),
\end{align}  
for an appropriately chosen tuning parameter $\gamma>0$, where $\rho_{\rm H}$
is the Huber function. Unfortunately, the cost function in the above  
minimization problem is not convex with respect to the parameter $\boldsymbol\mu$. 
This implies that general purpose guarantees available for approximating
solutions of convex programs are not applicable to \eqref{Hub}. To the best
of our knowledge, there is no efficient algorithm that provably approximates
$\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}^*$.

nodes.statement_short: IST approximates a nonconvex Huber-loss M-estimator for which no provably efficient algorithm is known.

nodes.name: Proof of the GSS risk bound
nodes.statement_short: Triangle-inequality decomposition plus three claims on the event $\Omega_\lambda$. Claim 1 (each selected set is at least half true support) is shown by contradiction with the minimality of $\widehat J$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality decomposition
nodes.statement:
Using the triangle inequality several times, we get
\begin{align}
\|\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GSS}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta)\|_2
    &\le \|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{\widehat S})-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S})\|_2+ \|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S})- \boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta_S)\|_2\\
    &\le \|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{\widehat S\setminus S})\|_2+\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus \widehat S})\|_2
			+ \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{S})\|_2 \phantom{\Big(}\\
    &\le \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{\widehat S\setminus S})\|_2+\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus \widehat S})\|_2
			+ \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{S})\|_2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split the error into three terms.

nodes.name: GSS error decomposition (line:3)
nodes.statement:
\|\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GSS}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta)\|_2
    &\le \|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{\widehat S})-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S})\|_2+ \|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S})- \boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta_S)\|_2\\
    &\le \|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{\widehat S\setminus S})\|_2+\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus \widehat S})\|_2
			+ \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{S})\|_2 \phantom{\Big(}\\
    &\le \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{\widehat S\setminus S})\|_2+\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus \widehat S})\|_2
			+ \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{S})\|_2.

nodes.name: Event Omega_lambda

J\subseteq [n]\Big\}.

nodes.name: State Claims 1-3
nodes.statement:
We will show that the following three claims are true for the tuning parameter $\lambda$ chosen as in the statement of the theorem.
\begin{description}\itemsep=5pt
\item[Claim 1:] On the event $\Omega_\lambda$, at least half of the elements of each $\widehat J_\ell$
belong to the true sparsity pattern $S$. Thus $|\widehat S|\le 2s$.
\item[Claim 2:] $\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus\widehat S})\|_2^2\le 12\sigma^2 s(p+\lambda s)$.
\item[Claim 3:] The probability of $\Omega_\lambda$ is close to $1$.
\end{description}

nodes.statement: Indeed,  the second term of the right hand side of \eqref{line:3} is bounded by $\sigma\sqrt{12s(p+\lambda s)}$ in view of Claim 2. The third term is bounded by $\sigma\sqrt{2s(p+\lambda s)}$ on the event $\Omega_\lambda$.

nodes.name: Bound first term
nodes.statement: Concerning the first term, we know that on $\Omega_\lambda$ it is bounded by $\sigma\sqrt{2|\widehat S|(p+\lambda |\widehat S|)}$. In view of Claim 1, $|\widehat S|\le 2s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a selected set with half its elements outside $S$ would have a smaller admissible subset.

nodes.name: Assume a bad selected set
nodes.statement: To prove the first claim, let us assume that there is a set $J$ among $\widehat J_1,\ldots,\widehat J_\ell$ and a subset $J_0\subset J$ of cardinality\footnote{To avoid uninteresting and irrelevant technicalities, we assume here that $|J|$ is even.} $|J|/2$ such that $J_0\subset S^c$.

nodes.statement_short: Additivity and the triangle inequality give $\|L(Y_J)\|^2<12\sigma^2|J|(p+\lambda|J|)$.

nodes.name: Contradiction chain for Claim 1
nodes.statement:
\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{J})\|_2^2
    & \le (\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{J\setminus J_0})\|_2+ \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{J_0})\|_2)^2 \phantom{\frac32} \\
    & \le \frac32\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{J\setminus J_0})\|_2^2+ 3\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\xi_{J_0})\|_2^2\\
    & < 9\sigma^2 |J|(p+\lambda |J|/2)+ 3\sigma^2 |J|(p+\lambda|J|/2) \phantom{\frac32}\\
    & < 12\sigma^2 |J|(p+\lambda|J|). \phantom{\frac32}

nodes.statement: This is in contradiction with the fact that $J$ is one of the sets $\widehat J_1,\ldots,\widehat J_L$. So, Claim 1 is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Contradicts the selection rule.

nodes.statement: The proof of Claim 2 is simpler. By construction, the set $S\setminus \widehat S$ is a subset of $I_L$, where $L$ is the number of steps performed by the algorithm. Since the algorithm terminated after the $L$th step, this means that $\mathcal I$ was empty, which implies  that $\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus\widehat S})\|_2^2\le 12\sigma^2 |S\setminus\widehat S|(p+\lambda|S\setminus\widehat S|) \le 12\sigma^2 s(p+\lambda s)$.

Since the algorithm terminated after the $L$th step, this means that $\mathcal I$ was empty, which implies  that $\|\boldsymbol L(\mathbf Y_{S\setminus\widehat S})\|_2^2\le 12\sigma^2 |S\setminus\widehat S|(p+\lambda|S\setminus\widehat S|) \le 12\sigma^2 s(p+\lambda s)$.

\mathbf P\big(\Omega_\lambda^c\big)
    &\le \sum_{k=1}^n {{n}\choose{k}} e^{-2\lambda k/3} = (1+e^{-2\lambda/3})^n-1.

nodes.name: Choice of lambda
nodes.statement: Therefore, for $\lambda = \nicefrac32\log(\nicefrac{2n}{\delta})$, we obtain that  $\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\Omega_\lambda^c\big)\le \delta$. This completes the proof of Claim~3 and of the theorem.

nodes.name: Proof of the GHT risk bound
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the error into stochastic error on the detected support, missed signal, and false detections; bound each in expectation.

nodes.name: Three-term decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the GHT error and apply the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: GHT error decomposition (decomposition)
nodes.statement:
\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GHT}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta)
		&= \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol Y\!_S-\boldsymbol\Theta) - \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol Y\!_{S\setminus S_\lambda} )+ \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol Y\!_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\\
		&= \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_S) - \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol Y\!_{S\setminus S_\lambda} )+ \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\\
		&= \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda}) - \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda} )+ \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S}).
nodes.label: decomposition

nodes.name: GHT three-term bound (ineq:2)
nodes.statement:
\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GHT}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta) \big\|_2 &\le \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2 +
	\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2 + \sigma\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda \setminus S})\|_2.
nodes.label: ineq:2

nodes.name: Stochastic error on support
nodes.statement_short: Bound via the spectral norm of the Gaussian submatrix (Lemma 9).

nodes.name: Spectral norm bound on detected noise
nodes.statement:
\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2 = \|\boldsymbol\Xi_{S}\mathbf 1_{S\cap S_\lambda}\|_2\le
 	\sqrt{s}\|\boldsymbol\Xi_{S}\|.

nodes.name: Expected detected noise (esperance_norm)
nodes.statement: \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2^2\big] \le 3s^2 + 3sp+12s.
nodes.label: esperance_norm

nodes.name: Missed signals
nodes.statement_short: Bound the contribution of undetected nonzero columns.

nodes.name: Missed signal bound
nodes.statement:
\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2&\le \sum_{i\in S} \|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2 \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|^2<\lambda^2	-2\sigma\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top \boldsymbol\xi_i-\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2} \\
	&\le s(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)^{1/2}+2\sigma\sum_{i\in S} |\eta_i| + \sigma\sum_{i\in S} \big| \|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2-p\, \big|^{1/2}.

nodes.name: Missed signal in expectation (eval_on_support)
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2^2]^{1/2}
	\le s(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)^{1/2}+2\sigma s + \sigma s (2p)^{1/4}.
nodes.label: eval_on_support

nodes.name: False detections
nodes.statement:
The third term in \eqref{ineq:2}
	corresponds to the Type II error in the problem of support estimation. Denoting
	$t=(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)/\sigma^2$, and using tail bounds for the chi-squared
	random variables (see \Cref{lemme_esperancechideux} below), we get
	\begin{align}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta}[\|\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda \setminus S}\|_2^2]
	    &= \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta}\bigg[\bigg\| \sum_{i\in S^c} \boldsymbol\xi_i\mathds{1}(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2\ge \lambda/\sigma)\bigg\|_2^2\bigg]\\
	    &= \sum_{i\in S^c}\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta}[\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2\mathds{1}(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2\ge p+t)]\\
	    &\le 	2n \big( pe^{-t^2/32p}\,\mathds{1}_{t< 4p} + t
	    e^{-t/4}\mathds{1}_{t \ge 4p}\big).
	\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Use the truncated $\chi^2$ moment bound (Lemma 6).

nodes.name: False detection noise
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta}[\|\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda \setminus S}\|_2^2]
	    &= \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta}\bigg[\bigg\| \sum_{i\in S^c} \boldsymbol\xi_i\mathds{1}(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2\ge \lambda/\sigma)\bigg\|_2^2\bigg]\\
	    &= \sum_{i\in S^c}\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta}[\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2\mathds{1}(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2\ge p+t)]\\
	    &\le 	2n \big( pe^{-t^2/32p}\,\mathds{1}_{t< 4p} + t
	    e^{-t/4}\mathds{1}_{t \ge 4p}\big).

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Plug in the threshold value and combine.

nodes.name: False detection bound
Proof of the GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
We define $\mathbf\Theta$ as the matrix with entries $\epsilon=\sigma p^{-1/4}$ in the first $s$ 
	columns and $0$ elsewhere. Using the inequality 
	$\forall a,b,~(a-b)^2\ge a^2/2-b^2$ and~\eqref{decomposition}, we get
	\begin{align}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GHT}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta) \big\|_2^2 \big]
			&\ge \frac12 \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S}) -
			\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] - \sigma^2\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} 
			\big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda}) \big\|_2^2\big].
	\end{align}
	Moreover, $\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})$ being centered and independent of 
	$\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})$, we can develop 
	\begin{align} \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S}) -
			\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] &= 
			\sigma^2\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\|  \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] +
			\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big].
	\end{align}
	First assume that $\lambda^2\ge \sigma^2 p + \sigma^2\sqrt{p}$ and focus on the second term in 
	the right-hand side of the last display. Using Jensen's inequality, we have
	\begin{align}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big]
	&\ge \big\| \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big]\big\|_2^2\\
	&=	p\epsilon^2s^2 \max_{i\in S}\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2<\lambda\big)^2\\
	&= s^2\sqrt{p}\max_{i\in S} \mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2<\lambda\big)^2.
	\end{align}
  On the other hand, since  ${\rm sgn}(\boldsymbol\xi_i^\top\boldsymbol\theta_i)$ 
	is a Rademacher random variable independent of $\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2$, for every $i\in S$, 
	we have
	\begin{equation}
	\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2^2<\lambda^2\big) 
		\ge 0.5\mathbf P\big(\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-\sigma^2p<\sigma^2\sqrt{p}-p\epsilon^2\big) 
		= 0.5\mathbf P\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-p<0\big).
	\end{equation}
	This last probability converges to $1/2$, so that it is larger than 
	$1/4$ for all $p$ large enough.
	
	In the other case, $\lambda^2< \sigma^2 p + \sigma^2\sqrt{p}$, we consider the first term:
	\begin{align}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\|  \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] 
		&= (n-s)p - (n-s)\mathbf E [\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2 \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2\le\lambda/\sigma}] \\
		&\ge (n-s)p - (n-s)(p+\sqrt{p}) \mathbf P\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-p\le\sqrt{p}\big).
	\end{align}
	The probability in the right-hand side converges to $\Phi(2^{-1/2})\le 0.8$, 
	so that for $p\ge 64$ and $s\le n/2$, we have
	\begin{equation}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\|  \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] 
	\ge (n-s) (0.2p-0.8p^{1/2}) \ge 0.05 np.
	\end{equation}
	
	Finally, according to \eqref{esperance_norm}, we have for $p$ large enough
	\begin{align}
		\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2^2\big] \le 3s^2 + 3sp+12s
		\le \frac{s^2\sqrt{p}}{65} + 3sp
	\end{align}	
	so that
	\begin{equation}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GHT}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta) \big\|_2^2\big] 
	\ge \frac{s^2\sqrt{p}}{65}\wedge(0.05np) - 3sp.
	\end{equation}
	We have to distinguish between two cases. If $s^2\sqrt{p}\le 196sp$, then the result holds in view of~\Cref{theorem_lowerbound}. In the opposite case, the result holds as long as $s\le n/61$.

			\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] - \sigma^2\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} 
			\big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda}) \big\|_2^2\big].

nodes.name: Bias-variance development (decomposition_preuve_lowerboundHT)
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \sigma\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S}) -
			\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] &= 
			\sigma^2\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\|  \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] +
			\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big].
nodes.label: decomposition_preuve_lowerboundHT

nodes.name: Case: large threshold
nodes.statement:
First assume that $\lambda^2\ge \sigma^2 p + \sigma^2\sqrt{p}$ and focus on the second term in 
	the right-hand side of the last display. Using Jensen's inequality, we have
	\begin{align}
	\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big]
	&\ge \big\| \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big]\big\|_2^2\\
	&=	p\epsilon^2s^2 \max_{i\in S}\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2<\lambda\big)^2\\
	&= s^2\sqrt{p}\max_{i\in S} \mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2<\lambda\big)^2.
	\end{align}
  On the other hand, since  ${\rm sgn}(\boldsymbol\xi_i^\top\boldsymbol\theta_i)$ 
	is a Rademacher random variable independent of $\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2$, for every $i\in S$, 
	we have
	\begin{equation}
	\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2^2<\lambda^2\big) 
		\ge 0.5\mathbf P\big(\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-\sigma^2p<\sigma^2\sqrt{p}-p\epsilon^2\big) 
		= 0.5\mathbf P\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-p<0\big).
	\end{equation}
	This last probability converges to $1/2$, so that it is larger than 
	$1/4$ for all $p$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality shows missed signals cost $s^2\sqrt p$.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big]
	&\ge \big\| \mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big]\big\|_2^2\\
	&=	p\epsilon^2s^2 \max_{i\in S}\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2<\lambda\big)^2\\
	&= s^2\sqrt{p}\max_{i\in S} \mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2<\lambda\big)^2.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
\mathbf P_{\mathbf\Theta}\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2^2<\lambda^2\big) 
		\ge 0.5\mathbf P\big(\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-\sigma^2p<\sigma^2\sqrt{p}-p\epsilon^2\big) 
		= 0.5\mathbf P\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-p<0\big).

nodes.name: Case: small threshold
nodes.statement_short: False detections cost order $np$.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\|  \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] 
		&= (n-s)p - (n-s)\mathbf E [\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2 \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2\le\lambda/\sigma}] \\
		&\ge (n-s)p - (n-s)(p+\sqrt{p}) \mathbf P\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_1\|_2^2-p\le\sqrt{p}\big).

nodes.name: Display in proof of GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\|  \boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S_\lambda\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] 
	\ge (n-s) (0.2p-0.8p^{1/2}) \ge 0.05 np.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the detected-noise term.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\|\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Xi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2^2\big] \le 3s^2 + 3sp+12s
		\le \frac{s^2\sqrt{p}}{65} + 3sp

nodes.name: Display in proof of GHT lower bound
nodes.statement:
\mathbf E_{\mathbf\Theta} \big[\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GHT}-\boldsymbol L(\mathbf\Theta) \big\|_2^2\big] 
	\ge \frac{s^2\sqrt{p}}{65}\wedge(0.05np) - 3sp.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: We have to distinguish between two cases. If $s^2\sqrt{p}\le 196sp$, then the result holds in view of~\Cref{theorem_lowerbound}. In the opposite case, the result holds as long as $s\le n/61$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Theorem 5 in the small-$s$ case.

nodes.name: Proof of the GST risk bound
nodes.statement_short: Split the GST error into approximation error, stochastic error on $S$ and on $S^c$, and bound each in $L_2$. The approximation error uses a two-case analysis of the signal-to-noise interaction.

nodes.name: Three-term decomposition
nodes.statement:
To ease notation, for every random vector
$X$ we write $\|X\|_{L_2}$ for $(\mathbf E[\|X\|_2^2])^{1/2}$. We first notice that
	\begin{align}
	\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GST}-\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta) &=  \sum_{i\in S} \boldsymbol\theta_i \bigg\{\bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}
	{(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+-1\bigg\} \qquad &(:=T_1)\\
	&+ \sigma\sum_{i\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i \bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+ \qquad &(:=T_2)\\
	&+ \sigma\sum_{i\not\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i \bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\sigma\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2-p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\qquad &(:=T_3),
	\end{align}	
	so that we only need to bound the expected squared norms of the three terms in the right-hand side. These three terms have the following meanings: the first one is the bias of estimation
or the approximation error, the second term is the stochastic error on the support $S$,
whereas the third term is the stochastic error on $S^\complement$.
nodes.statement_short: Write the error as approximation plus two stochastic terms.

nodes.name: GST error decomposition T1+T2+T3
nodes.statement:
\widehat{\boldsymbol L}{}^{\rm GST}-\boldsymbol L(\boldsymbol\Theta) &=  \sum_{i\in S} \boldsymbol\theta_i \bigg\{\bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}
	{(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+-1\bigg\} \qquad &(:=T_1)\\
	&+ \sigma\sum_{i\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i \bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\big(\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+ \qquad &(:=T_2)\\
	&+ \sigma\sum_{i\not\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i \bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\sigma\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2-p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\qquad &(:=T_3),

nodes.name: Approximation error
nodes.statement_short: Bound $T_1$.

nodes.name: Minkowski split
nodes.statement_short: Split $T_1$ and reuse the GHT bound for the first part.

nodes.name: Minkowski split of T1 (eqT1)
nodes.label: eqT1

nodes.name: First part of T1 (eqT1a)
nodes.statement:
\Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \boldsymbol\theta_i \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2^2\le\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2)
	}\Big\|_{L_2} \le \sigma s \big(\gamma+2 +  (2p)^{1/4}\big).
nodes.label: eqT1a

nodes.name: Define T_{1,i}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the per-column term.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GST bound
nodes.statement:
T_{1,i} = \frac{\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2\gamma\,\mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol Y\!_i\|_2^2>\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2)}}
	{(\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|^2_2+2\sigma\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top\boldsymbol\xi_i+\sigma^2\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2-p\big))^{1/2}} .

nodes.name: Case: small perturbation
nodes.statement:
The first case corresponds to 
	$\big|2\sigma\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top\boldsymbol\xi_i+\sigma^2\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2-p\big)\big|<\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2/2$. 
	In this case one easily checks that  $T_{1,i}\le \sqrt{2}\,\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Then $T_{1,i}\le\sqrt2\gamma$.

nodes.name: Case: large perturbation
nodes.statement:
In the second case, 
	$\big|2\sigma\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top\boldsymbol\xi_i+\sigma^2\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2-p\big)\big|\ge\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2/2$, 
	we have 
	\begin{equation}
		\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2/4 \le 2\sigma|\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top\boldsymbol\xi_i| \quad \text{or} \quad \|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2/4 \le 
		\sigma^2\big|\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2-p\big|.
	\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $T_{1,i}$ by noise terms and take $L_2$ norms.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GST bound
nodes.statement:
\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2/4 \le 2\sigma|\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top\boldsymbol\xi_i| \quad \text{or} \quad \|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2/4 \le 
		\sigma^2\big|\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2-p\big|.

Combine

nodes.name: Bound on T1 (eqT1c)
nodes.statement:
\|T_1\|_{L_2} &\le \sigma 
		s\gamma+2\sigma s + \sigma s(2p)^{1/4} + 8\sigma s+ 2\sigma s(2p)^{1/4}\\
		&= \sigma s\gamma+10\sigma s + 3\sigma s(2p)^{1/4}.
nodes.label: eqT1c

nodes.name: Stochastic error on S
nodes.statement_short: Wishart bound as in the GHT proof.

nodes.name: Display in proof of GST bound
nodes.statement: \|T_2\|_{L_2}^2 \le \sigma^2 s\mathbf E[\|\boldsymbol\Xi_S\|^2] \le \sigma^2(3s^2+3sp+12s).

nodes.name: Stochastic error on S complement
nodes.statement:
\paragraph{Evaluation of the stochastic error on $S^\complement$} For the third term,
	we write
	\begin{align}
		\|T_3\|_{L_2}^2=\sigma^2\bigg\| \sum_{i\not\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i
		\bigg(1-\frac{\gamma}{\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2-p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\bigg\|_{L_2}^2
			&= \sigma^2\sum_{i\not\in S} \bigg\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\bigg(1-\frac{\gamma}{(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2
				-p)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\bigg\|_{L_2}^2\\
			&\le \sigma^2\sum_{i\not\in S} \mathbf E\big[\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2 \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2> p+
			\gamma^2}\big].
	\end{align}
  We conclude by~\Cref{lemme_esperancechideux} that the last term satisfies
	\begin{equation}
		\|T_3\|_{L_2}^2\le 
		2n\sigma^2  \big( pe^{-\gamma^4/32p}\,\mathds{1}_{\gamma^2< 4p} +
		\gamma^2e^{-\gamma^2/4}\mathds{1}_{\gamma^2\ge 4p}\big).
	\end{equation}
	Using the fact that $\gamma^2= 4\log(1+n/s^2)\vee\big\{16p\log(1+n^2p/s^4)
	\big\}^{1/2}$ we arrive at
	\begin{align}
	\|T_3\|_{L_2}^2
	    &\le \sigma^2	\Big(8s^2\log(1+n/s^2)\Big)\vee \Big(2s^2\sqrt{p}
			\wedge 2np\Big).
	\end{align}
This completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $T_3$ with the truncated $\chi^2$ moment lemma.

nodes.name: Independence
nodes.statement:
For the third term,
	we write
	\begin{align}
		\|T_3\|_{L_2}^2=\sigma^2\bigg\| \sum_{i\not\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i
		\bigg(1-\frac{\gamma}{\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2-p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\bigg\|_{L_2}^2
			&= \sigma^2\sum_{i\not\in S} \bigg\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\bigg(1-\frac{\gamma}{(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2
				-p)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\bigg\|_{L_2}^2\\
			&\le \sigma^2\sum_{i\not\in S} \mathbf E\big[\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2 \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2> p+
			\gamma^2}\big].
	\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $T_3$ using independence.

nodes.statement:
\|T_3\|_{L_2}^2=\sigma^2\bigg\| \sum_{i\not\in S} \boldsymbol\xi_i
		\bigg(1-\frac{\gamma}{\big(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2-p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\bigg\|_{L_2}^2
			&= \sigma^2\sum_{i\not\in S} \bigg\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\bigg(1-\frac{\gamma}{(\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|^2_2
				-p)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\bigg\|_{L_2}^2\\
			&\le \sigma^2\sum_{i\not\in S} \mathbf E\big[\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2 \mathds{1}_{\|\boldsymbol\xi_i\|_2^2> p+
			\gamma^2}\big].

\|T_3\|_{L_2}^2\le

Proof of the group-lasso risk bound
nodes.statement_short: Basic inequality, cone condition on event $\mathcal A$, and the restricted-eigenvalue Lemma 4 for the projection $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Basic inequality
nodes.statement_short: Compare the objective at $\widehat\Theta$ and at $\Theta$.

nodes.statement: \big\| (\boldsymbol\Theta-\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta})\mathbf\Pi + \sigma\boldsymbol\Xi\mathbf\Pi \big\|_F^2 + \lambda \sum_{i=1}^n \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i\|_2 \le \sigma^2 \| \boldsymbol\Xi\mathbf\Pi \|_F^2 + \lambda \sum_{i=1}^n \|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2.

\| (\boldsymbol\Theta-\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta})\mathbf\Pi \|_F^2 &\le 2\sigma\sum_{n=1}^n 
	(\boldsymbol\Xi\mathbf\Pi)_i^\top(\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i) + \lambda \sum_{i=1}^n \big\{ \|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2 -

	&\le \frac\lambda2 \sum_{i=1}^n \Big\{ \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2
			+ 2 \|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2 - 2 \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i\|_2 \Big\} \\
	&\le \frac{3\lambda}2 \sum_{i\in S} \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2 -
			\frac\lambda2 \sum_{i\not\in S} \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2,

nodes.statement: \sum_{i\not\in S} \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2\le 3\sum_{i\in S} \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2.

nodes.statement: \|(\boldsymbol\Theta-\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta})\mathbf\Pi\|_F^2 \le \frac{3\lambda}2 \sqrt{s} \|\boldsymbol\Theta-\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}\|_F.

nodes.statement: \frac12 \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta\|_F^2 \le \frac{3\lambda}2 \sqrt{s} \|\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta\|_F,

nodes.name: Display in proof of group-lasso bound

nodes.name: Mean error
nodes.statement:
To show the second inequality,
	it suffices to remark that
	\begin{align}
	\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}-\boldsymbol\mu\|_2^2
			& \le \frac2{n^2}\|(\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta)\mathbf 1_n\|_2^2 +2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\
			& \le \frac{2}{n^2}\bigg(\sum_{i\in [n]}\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2\bigg)^2 
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\
			& \le \frac{2}{n^2}\bigg(4\sum_{i\in S}\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2\bigg)^2 
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\
			& \le \frac{32s}{n^2}\sum_{i\in S}\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2 
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\				
			& \le \frac{288s^2\lambda^2}{n^2}
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2.								
	\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the mean error through the column errors.

nodes.name: Display in proof of group-lasso bound
nodes.statement:
\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}-\boldsymbol\mu\|_2^2
			& \le \frac2{n^2}\|(\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta)\mathbf 1_n\|_2^2 +2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\
			& \le \frac{2}{n^2}\bigg(\sum_{i\in [n]}\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2\bigg)^2 
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\
			& \le \frac{2}{n^2}\bigg(4\sum_{i\in S}\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2\bigg)^2 
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\
			& \le \frac{32s}{n^2}\sum_{i\in S}\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2^2 
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2\\				
			& \le \frac{288s^2\lambda^2}{n^2}
				+2\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2.

nodes.name: Chi-square noise
nodes.statement:
To complete the proof, we use the fact that $n\|\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Xi)\|_2^2$ is a $\chi^2(p)$
random variable, which implies that with probability at least $1-\delta/2$ it is bounded
from above by $2p+4\log(2/\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the averaged noise by a $\chi^2$ tail.

nodes.name: Proof of the one-step improvement proposition
nodes.statement:
To ease notation, we set $\sigma_{n,p}^2 = (n-1)\sigma^2p/n$, 
$w_i=\big( 1-\sigma\gamma/\sqrt{(\|\boldsymbol Z_i \|_2^2-\sigma_{n,p}^2)_+} \big)_+$,
$\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n = \widetilde{\boldsymbol L}_n-\boldsymbol L_n(\boldsymbol\Theta)$ and $\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i= \boldsymbol\xi_i-\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}$.
Then,
	\begin{equation}
		\boldsymbol Z_i = \boldsymbol\theta_i + \widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n + \sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i.
	\end{equation}	
We first show that with high probability the weights $w_i$
vanish outside the support $S$.

\begin{lemma} In the event $\Omega_1\cap \Omega_2$, where
\begin{align}
\Omega_2 &= \Big\{\max_i\big|\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2-(1-\nicefrac1n)p\big|\le 0.5\gamma^2\Big\},
\end{align}
we have $w_i=0$ for every $i\not\in S$. Furthermore, under the condition
$\gamma^2 > 4\log(4n/\delta)+4 \{p\log(4n/\delta)\}^{1/2}$, the probability of
$\Omega_2$ is at least $1-\delta/2$.
\end{lemma}

	Using equation~\eqref{Z0} and the fact that $w_i=0$ for every
	$i\not\in S$ in the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, we get	
	\begin{align}
	\boldsymbol L(\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta)
		&= \sum_{i=1}^n \boldsymbol Z_i w_i-\sum_{i\in S} \boldsymbol\theta_i
		= \sum_{i\in S} \big(\boldsymbol Z_i w_i -\boldsymbol\theta_i\big).
	\end{align}
	Replacing $\boldsymbol Z_i$ by $\boldsymbol\theta_i + \widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n + \sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i$ and using the
	triangle inequality, we obtain
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol L(\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta) \|_2
		&\le \Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \big(\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\big) (w_i-1)\Big\|_2 +
			\Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \big(\boldsymbol Z_i-\boldsymbol\theta_i\big)+\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i(w_i-1)\Big\|_2\\
		&\le \sum_{i\in S} \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2 |w_i-1| +
			\Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \big(\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n
			+ \sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i w_i\big)\Big\|_2\\
		&\le \sum_{i\in S} \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2 |w_i-1| +
			{s}\big\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\big\|_2
			+ \sigma\Big\|\sum_{i\in S}\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i w_i\Big\|_2. \end{align}	
	We will now evaluate the first and the third terms of the right-hand side.	
	\begin{lemma} There is a sequence of standard Gaussian random variables 
	$\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_n$ such that in the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, it holds
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol Z_i - \sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2|w_i-1|
		\le 2\sigma|\eta_i| + \big\{|2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n|\big\}^{1/2} + 
			1.96\sigma\gamma. \end{align}
	\end{lemma}

	Let us introduce the $p\times s$ matrix $\boldsymbol\Xi_S = [\,\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i; i\in S\,]$ (the matrix
	obtained by concatenating the vectors $\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i$ with subscript $i$ running over $S$).
	Using the H\"older inequality, one can check that
	\begin{align}
	\sum_{i\in S}\big\{2\sigma|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n|\big\}^{1/2}
			&\le \sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \bigg(\sum_{i\in S} |\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n|^2
				\bigg)^{1/4}\\
			&= \sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \|\boldsymbol\Xi_S^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2^{1/2}\\
			&\le \sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \|\boldsymbol\Xi_S\|^{1/2}\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2^{1/2}. \end{align}
	Finally, the third term in the right-hand side of \eqref{Z1} can be bounded as follows:
	\begin{equation}
		\Big\| \sum_{i\in S}\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_iw_i\Big\|_2 = \|\boldsymbol\Xi_S \boldsymbol w\|_2\le \sqrt{s}\,\|\boldsymbol\Xi_S\|. \end{equation}
	Combining \eqref{Z1}, \eqref{Z2}, \eqref{Z3} and \eqref{Z4}, we arrive at
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol L(\widehat{\boldsymbol\Theta}-\boldsymbol\Theta) \|_2
		&\le 2\sigma\sum_{i\in S}\big(|\eta_i| + \big\{2\sigma|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n^\top 
		\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i|\big\}^{1/2}\big) +1.96\,\sigma s\gamma
			+ {s}\big\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\big\|_2  + \sigma\sqrt{s}\,\|\boldsymbol\Xi_S\|\\
		&\le 2\sigma\sum_{i\in S}|\eta_i|+2.21\,\sigma s\gamma+\sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \|\boldsymbol\Xi_S\|^{1/2}

nodes.name: Proof of the recursion lemma
nodes.statement:
We prove by inductive reasoning that for every $k$ we have
		$\epsilon_k^2\le p$ and \eqref{recursion:claim}. This is trivially
		true for $k=0$. Assume that these claims hold true for some given 
		value $k$. Let us check them for the value $k+1$. 
		From recursion \eqref{eq:recursion}, one can infer that  
		\begin{align} \epsilon_{k+1} \le \frac{16.5s}{n}(\epsilon_k\vee p^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2}) +a
				\le \frac{33s}{n}(\epsilon_k\vee p^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2})\vee 2a.
		\end{align}
		The conditions of the lemma directly imply that $\epsilon_{k+1}^2\le p$. Therefore,
		\begin{align} \epsilon_{k+1} \le \frac{33sp^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2}}{n}\vee 2a.
		\end{align}
		Applying inequality \eqref{recursion:claim}, we get the claim.
		
		One can note that even in the case $\epsilon_k>\sqrt{p}$, we get 
		from \eqref{eq:recursion1a} that
		\begin{align} \epsilon_{k+1} \le \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_k +a.
		\end{align}
		Therefore, if the preliminary estimator is not good enough to guarantee that 
		$\epsilon_0\le \sqrt{p}$, after a number of steps at most logarithmic in 
		$\epsilon_0/(\sqrt{p}-2a)$, we will get an error $\epsilon_k$ smaller than
		$\sqrt{p}$.

nodes.name: Proof that weights vanish outside the support
nodes.statement:
It follows from the definition of $w_i$ that, for every $i\not\in S$, $w_i>0$ 
		is equivalent to
		$$
				\|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i+\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2^2 > \sigma^2(p+\gamma^2).
		$$
		In view of the triangle inequality, this implies that
		$$
				\sigma\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2 + \|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2 > \sigma\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}.
		$$			
		In the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, the last inequality implies
		$$		
				\sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2} + \frac{\gamma^2}{4\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}}> \sqrt{p+\gamma^2}.
		$$
		It is easy to see that the last inequality is never true, implying thus that
		$w_i=0$. Indeed,
		\begin{align}
				\sqrt{p+\gamma^2} -\sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2}  
					& = \frac{0.5\gamma^2}{\sqrt{p+\gamma^2} +\sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2}}\\
					& > \frac{0.5\gamma^2}{\sqrt{p+\gamma^2} +\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}}
					= \frac{\gamma^2}{4\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}}.
		\end{align}
		The fact that the probability of $\Omega_2$ is at least $1-\delta/2$ is
		a consequence of the tail bound of a chi-squared random variable and the
		union bound.

		$$
		In view of the triangle inequality, this implies that
		$$
				\sigma\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2 + \|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2 > \sigma\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}.
		$$

nodes.name: Proof of the per-column shrinkage bound
nodes.statement:
The definition of $\boldsymbol Z_i$ yields
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2|w_i-1|  &= \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2 \min\bigg\{ 1,
	\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\big(\|\boldsymbol Z_i\|^2_2-\sigma_{n,p}^2\big)^{1/2}_+} \bigg\}.
	\end{align}
	Let us introduce the random variables $\eta_i = 
	\frac{n}{n-1}\boldsymbol\theta_i^\top\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i/\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2$. It is clear that $\eta_i$ is Gaussian
	with zero mean and unit variance. Repeated use of the triangle inequality leads to
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol Z_i\|_2^2
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 + 2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top(\boldsymbol\theta_i
		+\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n) \\
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2|\eta_i|
		+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\\
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2
		|\eta_i| -2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\\
		&\ge (\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2-\sigma|\eta_i|)^2 -\sigma^2\eta_i^2 + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2
		-2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n.
	\end{align}
	One can check the following simple fact: if $a,b,c,d>0$ then
	$$
	a\min\Big(1,\frac{d}{\{(a-b)^2-c\}_+^{1/2}}\Big)\le  b + d+\sqrt{c_+}.
	$$
	Taking in this inequality $a = \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2$, 
	$c = \sigma^2\eta_i^2 - \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2
		+2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|-2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n + 
		\sigma^2_{n,p}$, $b=\sigma|\eta_i|$ and $d=\sigma\gamma$, we arrive at
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2|w_i-1|
		&\le 2\sigma|\eta_i| + \sigma\gamma+ \|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2\\
		&\qquad+\sqrt{(\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2)_+}
		+\sqrt{(2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n -\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2^2)_+}.
	\end{align}
	In the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, we upper bound $\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2$ and
	$|\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2|$ respectively by $0.25\sigma\gamma$ 
	and $0.5\sigma^2\gamma^2$. This leads to the claim of the lemma.

		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 + 2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top(\boldsymbol\theta_i
		+\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n) \\
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2|\eta_i|
		+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\\
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2
		|\eta_i| -2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\\
		&\ge (\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2-\sigma|\eta_i|)^2 -\sigma^2\eta_i^2 + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2
		-2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n.
	\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce Gaussian $\eta_i$ and lower-bound $\|Z_i\|^2$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on Z_i norm
nodes.statement:
\|\boldsymbol Z_i\|_2^2
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 + 2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top(\boldsymbol\theta_i
		+\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n) \\
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\boldsymbol\theta_i\|_2|\eta_i|
		+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\\
		&\ge \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2  + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2
		|\eta_i| -2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\\
		&\ge (\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2-\sigma|\eta_i|)^2 -\sigma^2\eta_i^2 + \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2
		-2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n.

nodes.name: Elementary inequality
nodes.statement:
One can check the following simple fact: if $a,b,c,d>0$ then
	$$
	a\min\Big(1,\frac{d}{\{(a-b)^2-c\}_+^{1/2}}\Big)\le  b + d+\sqrt{c_+}.
	$$
	Taking in this inequality $a = \|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2$, 
	$c = \sigma^2\eta_i^2 - \|\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2
		+2\sigma\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2|\eta_i|-2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n + 
		\sigma^2_{n,p}$, $b=\sigma|\eta_i|$ and $d=\sigma\gamma$, we arrive at
	\begin{align}
	\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2|w_i-1|
		&\le 2\sigma|\eta_i| + \sigma\gamma+ \|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2\\
		&\qquad+\sqrt{(\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2)_+}
		+\sqrt{(2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n -\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2^2)_+}.
	\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inequality $a\min(1,d/\{(a-b)^2-c\}_+^{1/2})\le b+d+\sqrt{c_+}$.

nodes.name: Per-column bound before event
nodes.statement:
\|\boldsymbol Z_i-\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2|w_i-1|
		&\le 2\sigma|\eta_i| + \sigma\gamma+ \|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2\\
		&\qquad+\sqrt{(\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2)_+}
		+\sqrt{(2\sigma\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i^\top\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n -\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2^2)_+}.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
In the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, we upper bound $\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol\Delta}_n\|_2$ and
	$|\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar{\boldsymbol\xi}_i\|_2^2|$ respectively by $0.25\sigma\gamma$ 
	and $0.5\sigma^2\gamma^2$. This leads to the claim of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the remaining terms on the event.
